newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich guard faces Texas drunk driving charge.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich guard faces Texas drunk driving charge.

text.p: A U.S. Capitol police officer who guards Newt Gingrich was charged with drunk driving in Texas last month when he was arranging security for a trip by the House speaker, police said Tuesday.

John Erickson, 29, of Crofton, Maryland, has taken personal leave while Capitol police conduct an internal investigation in Washington. He was to be arraigned July 21 in San Antonio on the drunk driving charge, police said.
Erickson and a companion were found parked on a roadside at about 3:25 a.m. June 28 in a government-rented convertible.

"He was in the driver's seat with his head on his chest, passed out, extremely intoxicated, his speech was slurred," San Antonio police spokeswoman Sandy Perez read from a police arrest report. Erickson refused to take a breath test and was released after spending several hours in jail, she said.
Capitol police Sgt. Dan Nichols said Erickson, a member of the force since 1990, would be placed on restricted duty when he returns from leave and faces disciplinary action by the department.
"He was on official business but he was off duty at the time of the arrest," Nichols said. "Regardless, it's a violation of our policy."
